verdict.rationale: Conductor is a Mac app that runs many coding agents in parallel, with each workspace getting its own diff and review path, and it helps you review the diff before opening a PR. That covers the core of the story, but no source describes the diff viewer's visual presentation or a literal side-by-side layout of sessions. Missing for 10: documentation of the visual diff UI (inline/split view, commenting), evidence of a side-by-side multi-session layout rather than sidebar switching, independent hands-on corroboration of diff review.

support.subject: As a developer, I can review diffs visually and run multiple sessions side by side in a desktop app

citations.quote: Conductor is a Mac app that lets you run many coding agents in parallel on your codebase.
Each task gets its own workspace, branch, files, terminal, diff, and review path.
When the work is ready, Conductor helps you review the diff, open a pull request, merge, and archive the workspace.
Conductor lets you run Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode in parallel.
